raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through as I walk my fields...

---

*I'm 69 now, and I've been working this little piece of ground for most of my life. Just 3.5 mu — not much, but it feeds us and gives a bit of cash. My wife and I are the only ones here; the kids send money sometimes but they've got their own lives in town. So I can't be running around doing fancy things. I do what I've always done, same as my neighbors.*

**On the wheat (already in the ground since October):**

I put the wheat in last fall, middle of October like always. Before planting I spread two bags of the compound fertilizer — the 15-15-15 one from the supply shop — over the whole 3.5 mu. That's about how much the old man next door uses too. I ran the rotary tiller (hired the fellow with the tractor, 60 yuan per mu, my back can't do it anymore) and drilled the seed. I saved some seed from last year's crop and bought a little more to mix in.

Now it's April, the wheat is standing up nice at jointing stage. Time to put down a bag of urea as the topdress — I'll scatter it by hand before I open the well valve. Then water it in. I'll water again around the time the grain is filling out, maybe end of May. If it rains good I skip one. The water costs money — the pump runs on electricity and they meter it now.

For bugs and weeds, I'll buy a bottle of the weed spray from the shop in town, that's usually enough. Don't usually need the bug spray unless I see aphids bad.

I'm hoping for around 380 kg per mu. Last year I got a bit over that, year before was dry so less. It depends on the weather in May mostly.

**On the maize (coming up after wheat):**

Soon as I cut the wheat in early June — I hire the combine, 60 yuan per mu, they come through the village — I'll plant maize right into the stubble. No time to till, got to get it in within a few days or you lose the growing season. I use the hybrid seed, the one everyone around here plants, Zhengdan or similar. Costs more than saving seed but you can't save hybrid seed, doesn't work right.

I'll put one bag of compound down at planting with the seed, then wait till the maize is about waist-high — big bell stage, when it's really jumping — and topdress a bag of urea. Scatter it between the rows before a rain or irrigation.

Usually I water the maize once, in July if it's dry. Summer rains help a lot. I'll spray herbicide once when the maize is small, that's it.

Hoping for maybe 430 kg per mu. The maize has been pretty reliable.

**Money worries:**

Every bag of fertilizer is about 100-120 yuan. Adds up fast even on 3.5 mu. Custom machinery takes another chunk. I don't borrow — never have, never will — so I only spend what I've got. That's why I don't put on extra fertilizer "just in case" like some of the bigger farmers. If I had 30 mu I might think different, but on 3.5 mu every yuan matters.
